original: z opačnej strany matriky prípisy szatmárskeho biskupa od r. 1837-1840
translation: from the other end of the register, notes by the bishop of Szatmár from 1837 to 1840
why: The Senné parish copied its bishop's circulars into a blank book in the 1830s, then turned the book over a generation later and began the marriage register of 1863 from the other end.

original: Not quoted: a row of a table. Vysoká, 230 houses, 0 inhabitants.
translation: The Slovak state's list for 1940 gives Vysoká 230 houses and nobody living in them.
why: A printing or data fault, and the only evidence this repo has that the village was in Slovakia that year.

original: Not held; taken from the village chronicle as summarised.
translation: Lightning struck the Greek Catholic church of Iňačovce on 6 July 1929, and fire followed on 1 April 1930.
why: The parish archive was hit twice in nine months. Yet the baptism book for 1870-1898 was still being written in four years later.
Written in Slovak into the remarks column of a Latin baptism entry of 1872. Somebody closed the record sixty-two years after opening it, in the third official language the book had seen.

original: Not held; from the municipal history as summarised.
translation: Senné fished from dugout boats into the 20th century and kept geese in flocks of thousands until 1975.
why: The village the records describe was half water. It explains the fishponds reserve that fills its fields today.
One letter from Szenna (Senné) and identical to Szinna (Snina). Three villages in three counties that an index can fold into one.

translation: One cottar household of Jesztreb at seven house numbers between 1864 and 1885.
why: Either the family moved every three years or the village could not settle on its numbering. Nobody has found out which.

original: approximately 30 families purchased a piece of property for $350
translation: The founding of the Greek Catholic parish at Bradenville, Pennsylvania, in 1902.
why: The same coal town, in the same year, appears in the residence column of a Reformed baptism book kept for a village of a few hundred people on the Uh.

original: Not held; from a study of the 1734 visitation as summarised.
translation: The Catholic priest of Senné in 1734 spent most of his teaching on Rebrín, a Reformed village, while Reformed preachers held three of his other filials under the landlord's protection.
why: A parish priest whose flock mostly belonged to someone else.

original: Not held; from the municipal history as summarised.
translation: About 600 cows died in Senné in 1940, and the harvests failed for two years after.
why: A village of 171 houses losing 600 cows is most of its wealth gone in a season.
